detailed_description: The Border Radius Generator is a specialized tool for creating precise CSS border-radius values using a WYSIWYG editor. It enables developers to define both horizontal and vertical radii for each corner of an element, supporting pixel, percentage, and CSS variable inputs. Technically, it generates standardized shorthand notation (e.g., 10px / 20px) while maintaining control over individual corner properties (border-top-left-radius, border-bottom-right-radius, etc.). This tool addresses the complexity of visualizing non-uniform curves and ensures pixel-perfect control for implementing modern UI designs like card components, floating panels, and custom buttons. Developers can manipulate elliptical curves through interactive handles, view real-time element rendering, and access the underlying CSS code for immediate implementation. The tool's technical value lies in its ability to synchronize visual adjustments with CSS syntax, eliminating guesswork in responsive design scenarios where fluid border radii are required.
usage_steps: Adjust horizontal and vertical radius sliders to set base curvature values for all corners simultaneously.
Click individual corner handles to modify specific radii independently while maintaining visual proportion.
Enable the 'Sync Corners' button to apply uniform values across all four corners instantly.
Input custom CSS variables (e.g., var(--radius)) in numeric fields to create theme-aware stylesheets.
Toggle between 'px' and '%' units to define relative or absolute border curvature measurements.
Copy the generated CSS code snippet from the output panel and apply it to target elements in your stylesheet.
usage_examples: Designing a pill-shaped navigation tab with fully rounded ends using 999px radius values and horizontal symmetry.
Creating a card component with 8px top corners and 0px bottom corners to match Material Design specifications.
Implementing a circular profile avatar with 50% border-radius while maintaining aspect ratio in responsive layouts.
Producing a diagonal ribbon effect by applying contrasting radii values (e.g., 15px 5px / 30px 10px) to a rotated element.
